clinical_text: 32-year-old woman presenting with progressive proximal muscle weakness over 8 months, exercise intolerance and bilateral ptosis. She reports two episodes of transient right-sided weakness with headache in the past year, each resolving within 48 hours. Height 152 cm, below the 3rd centile for her family. Serum lactate 4.2 mmol/L (reference 0.5-2.2), resting. Creatine kinase 480 U/L. Thyroid function normal. Brain MRI: bilateral parieto-occipital signal change not conforming to a single vascular territory. Muscle biopsy: ragged red fibres on modified Gomori trichrome, subsarcolemmal accumulation of mitochondria on succinate dehydrogenase staining. No family history of neuromuscular disease; mother reports migraine and early hearing loss.
gold_synonyms: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes
notes: Free-text narrative with laboratory values, imaging and histology. Exercises the knowledge and analogy pathways: the ragged red fibres and elevated lactate are retrievable defining features, while the stroke-like episodes distinguish MELAS from a generic mitochondrial myopathy.
